suggestions.title: Load large data files asynchronously to unblock rendering

suggestions.description: An extremely long animation frame of 19.4 seconds freezes the main thread at page load, causing a severe INP issue. - Apply CSS to the '#home' selector to reserve space for it before its content loads. Use a `min-height` or the `aspect-ratio` property to prevent the container from collapsing. For example, add `min-height: 1261px;` or `aspect-ratio: 601 / 1261;` to your stylesheet for the `#home` element.

suggestions.title: Prevent massive layout shift by reserving space for the #home container

suggestions.description: At least 17 images, including LCP candidates like 'artistslidernew.jpg' and 'lineup6.jpg', are missing `width` and `height` attributes. This forces the browser to reflow the page layout after the images download, causing significant and repeated layout shifts (CLS).

suggestions.title: Add width and height attributes to images to prevent layout shifts

suggestions.description:
The legacy JavaScript font-rendering library, Cufon, is a major performance bottleneck. It uses two render-blocking scripts (`cufon-yui.js`, `League_Gothic_400-League_Gothic_400.font.js`) that delay LCP, runs a 2.4-second long task that freezes the page (INP), and swaps in fonts after render, causing significant layout shifts (CLS).

Multiple JavaScript files, including `jquery.nivo.slider.pack.js`, `superfish.js`, and `site.js`, are loaded synchronously in the `<head>`. They are not required for the initial paint and block the browser from rendering the page, which delays FCP and LCP.
suggestions.implementation:
- Remove the Cufon implementation entirely. Delete the `<script>` tags for `cufon-yui.js` and `League_Gothic_400-League_Gothic_400.font.js` from the HTML `<head>`. Replace it with a modern CSS `@font-face` rule in your stylesheet to load the 'League Gothic' font (preferably in WOFF2 format). Ensure the `font-family` declaration includes a fallback system font (e.g., `font-family: 'League Gothic', sans-serif;`) and use `font-display: swap;` in the `@font-face` rule to prevent render blocking.
- Add the `defer` attribute to the `<script>` tags for all non-essential JavaScript files loaded in the `<head>`. This instructs the browser to download them without blocking rendering and to execute them only after the HTML is fully parsed. Specifically target: `jquery.nivo.slider.pack.js`, `superfish.js`, `site.js`, `ui.tabs.js`, and `admin.js`.
suggestions.title: Replace legacy Cufon font rendering to fix LCP, CLS, and INP

suggestions.description:
The application is loading over 5.5 MB of unused JavaScript, primarily from the monolithic `sap/m/library-preload.js` (3 MB unused) and `sap/ui/core/library-preload.js` (1.9 MB unused) files. This significantly increases download, parse, and execution time, blocking rendering and interactivity, which is a root cause of poor LCP, TBT, and INP.

The CSS file `library.css` from the SAP UI5 CDN is 133 KB and is render-blocking. It takes over 750ms to download on a mobile connection, delaying the First Contentful Paint and LCP because the browser must wait for it to be fully downloaded and parsed.
suggestions.implementation:
- Configure the SAP UI5 build process, using the UI5 Tooling, to generate custom, optimized bundles. This involves creating a dependency graph of your application and including only the specific modules and controls that are actually used. This will produce smaller `Component-preload.js` or custom `library-preload.js` files, drastically reducing the initial JavaScript payload.
- Use the UI5 theme build tools to generate a custom theme for your application. This process will create a much smaller `library.css` file that includes only the styles required by the components your application actually uses, significantly reducing its size and the time it spends blocking render.
suggestions.title: Reduce JavaScript payload by removing unused SAP UI5 modules

suggestions.description: A single synchronous script execution, initiated by `sap-ui-core.js`, blocks the main thread for nearly 8 seconds. This long task freezes the browser, delaying First Contentful Paint, Largest Contentful Paint, and making the page completely unresponsive, resulting in a very high Interaction to Next Paint (INP).
suggestions.implementation: Profile the application's startup script to identify the specific functions responsible for the 8-second long task. Refactor this synchronous initialization logic by breaking it into smaller, asynchronous chunks. Yield to the main thread between units of work using `setTimeout(..., 0)` to allow the browser to process rendering updates and user input.
suggestions.title: Break up 8-second script execution in `sap-ui-core.js`

suggestions.description: The main SAP UI5 framework script, `sap-ui-core.js`, is loaded synchronously in the document `<head>`. This blocks the browser from parsing the rest of the HTML and rendering any content until the script is fully downloaded and executed, which takes over 1.3 seconds. This directly delays both FCP and LCP.
suggestions.implementation: Modify the `<script>` tag for `sap-ui-core.js`. Instead of a standard synchronous load, use the framework's built-in asynchronous bootstrap mechanism by adding the attribute `data-sap-ui-async="true"`. This allows the browser to render the page while the UI5 framework loads in the background.
suggestions.title: Load the main SAP UI5 script asynchronously to unblock rendering

suggestions.description:
The script `main.js` is loaded synchronously in the document `<head>`, forcing the browser to download and execute it for over 200ms before any content can be rendered. This directly delays First Contentful Paint and Largest Contentful Paint.

Two large stylesheets, `bulma.min.css` (190KB) and `font-awesome.min.css`, are loaded synchronously in the `<head>`, blocking the rendering of the page for a combined total of over 630ms. This is a primary cause of slow First Contentful Paint and Largest Contentful Paint.
suggestions.implementation:

Change `<script src="https://00btweb.github.io/js/main.js"></script>` to `<script src="https://00btweb.github.io/js/main.js" defer></script>`. Then, modify the `<link>` tags for `bulma.min.css` and `font-awesome.min.css` to load asynchronously using the pattern: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="..." media="print" onload="this.media='all'">`.

suggestions.description: A 1.2-second long task, originating from the `main.js` script, freezes the main thread at the very beginning of the page load. This long-running script execution blocks rendering, delays interactivity, and significantly harms INP and LCP.
suggestions.implementation: Profile the execution of `main.js` using browser developer tools to pinpoint the specific function(s) causing the 1.2-second task. Refactor this code to break the work into smaller chunks, each taking less than 50ms. Use `setTimeout`, `requestAnimationFrame`, or other yielding techniques to return control to the main thread between chunks.
suggestions.title: Break up 1.2-second long task in main.js

suggestions.description: Multiple large, unoptimized images are served from `images2.imgbox.com`, a slow third-party domain using HTTP/1.1. Download times for individual images like `UjlY4SgF_o.jpg` (495 KB) exceed 4 seconds, severely delaying LCP and creating a high risk of layout shifts.

Before uploading, resize images to their maximum display dimensions and compress them using modern, efficient formats like WebP or AVIF. suggestions.description: The `jquery.js` file is 575 KB, but 138 KB (24%) of its code is unused. Downloading, parsing, and executing this large file contributes to long tasks (over 86ms) and significantly delays LCP and interactivity (INP).

` that uses a CSS background image with a standard `` tag. It has a high Time to First Byte (TTFB) of over 150ms for static files and, due to its lack of HTTP/2 support, creates extreme request queuing where image downloads are blocked for over 2 seconds. This severely delays LCP and FCP.
suggestions.implementation: Replace the basic Python development server with a production-grade web server like Nginx or Apache. Configure it to use HTTP/2, which enables request multiplexing and will resolve the connection limit bottleneck, drastically reducing resource load times.
suggestions.title: Upgrade Web Server to Eliminate Request Queuing and High TTFB

suggestions.description:

suggestions.implementation:
- Use the browser's performance profiler to identify the script and function responsible for the 878ms long animation frame at the start of the page load. Refactor this synchronous, blocking code into smaller, asynchronous tasks using `setTimeout`, `requestAnimationFrame`, or by moving it into a web worker to unblock the main thread and allow the page to render sooner.
- Use the browser performance profiler to investigate the script execution around the 3.9-second mark. Identify the specific jQuery-driven function causing the 99ms task. Refactor this operation to yield to the main thread by breaking it into smaller chunks using `setTimeout` or `requestIdleCallback`.

suggestions.description: The single-threaded Python development server is causing a request queue, resulting in high Time to First Byte (TTFB) and delayed downloads for all assets. HAR analysis shows assets like 'sha1.js' and 'portal.js' have an artificial TTFB of ~190ms due to this bottleneck, which cascades to delay FCP and LCP.
suggestions.implementation: Replace the current Python `SimpleHTTPServer` with a modern development server capable of handling concurrent requests. Recommended options include Node.js `http-server` (`npx http-server`) or Caddy. This change will allow the browser to download resources in parallel, significantly reducing overall load time.

suggestions.description:
Three render-blocking JavaScript files (`script.js`, `theme.js`, `portal.js`) are parsed and executed in the `<head>`, delaying First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Largest Contentful Paint (LCP). Performance observers show these scripts contribute over 800ms of blocking time.

Multiple large stylesheets (`index.css`, `index_carbon.css`, `portal.css`) are loaded synchronously in the `<head>`, blocking the entire page from rendering until they are fully downloaded. The file `index.css` alone takes over 850ms to load, significantly delaying FCP and LCP.

A 64KB inline `<script>` block in the HTML is parsed and executed synchronously, blocking the main thread and delaying rendering. Because it's inline, it cannot be cached by the browser, leading to repeated processing on every page visit.
suggestions.implementation:
- To prevent these scripts from blocking the HTML parser, add the `defer` attribute to their respective `<script>` tags in the document's `<head>`. This will cause the browser to download them in parallel and execute them only after the document has been fully parsed.
- Identify the minimal CSS rules required to render the content visible in the initial viewport (above-the-fold). Inline these 'critical' styles into a `<style>` block in the `<head>`. Load the full stylesheets (`index.css`, `index_carbon.css`, `portal.css`) asynchronously by adding `media="print" onload="this.media='all'"` to their `<link>` tags.
- Move the entire 64KB of JavaScript code from the inline `<script>` block into a new, external file (e.g., `init-bundle.js`). Replace the inline script with a `<script src="init-bundle.js" defer></script>` tag. This change enables browser caching and prevents the script from blocking the initial page render.
suggestions.title: Defer Non-Critical JavaScript to Unblock Rendering

suggestions.description: A very long task lasting 1077ms is blocking the main thread at the very beginning of the page load. This freezes the browser, delaying any user interaction (hurting INP) and preventing the page from rendering content quickly (hurting FCP and LCP).

suggestions.description:
First Contentful Paint (FCP) and LCP are delayed because multiple large CSS files are blocking rendering in the document `<head>`. The files `app.modern.css` (46kb) and `app.modern.fingerprint.css` (26kb) must be fully downloaded and parsed before the page can display any content, taking over 900ms. Analysis shows that a large portion of the CSS rules are not needed for the initial viewport.

LCP is delayed because the browser has to download, parse, and execute the render-blocking scripts `app.js` and `app.fingerprint.js` before it can render the page's main content. These scripts block the rendering path, even if their functionality is not required for the initial view.

A large inline `<script>` block of 65KB is blocking HTML parsing and delaying FCP and LCP. Code coverage analysis shows that 37KB (57%) of this code is either completely unused or only executed after the initial page render. This non-critical JavaScript is needlessly parsed and compiled on the critical path.
suggestions.implementation:
- Identify the critical CSS rules required for rendering the content visible in the initial viewport (above-the-fold). Inline these critical rules directly into a `<style>` block in the document `<head>`. Load the full stylesheets (`app.modern.css`, `app.modern.fingerprint.css`) asynchronously by adding `media="print"` and `onload="this.media='all'"` to their `<link>` tags, or by using another non-blocking loading method.
- Add the `defer` attribute to the `<script>` tags for `app.js` and `app.fingerprint.js`. This will instruct the browser to download the scripts in parallel with HTML parsing and execute them only after the document has been fully parsed, removing them from the critical rendering path.
- Identify the 37KB of unused or deferrable code within the large inline script (`inline@0`). Extract this code and move it into a separate external JavaScript file. Load this new file using a `<script>` tag with the `defer` attribute. This will remove the non-critical code from the render-blocking path.
suggestions.title: Defer non-critical CSS to accelerate page rendering

suggestions.description:
A very long animation frame at the start of page load is blocking the main thread for up to 1532ms, severely impacting Interaction to Next Paint (INP), Total Blocking Time (TBT), and delaying First Contentful Paint (FCP). This blocking is caused by a long-running script executed by `app.js` immediately upon loading.

A synchronous data-fetching request to `api.github.com` is delaying the LCP by at least 505ms due to its high Time to First Byte (TTFB). This network request appears on the critical path, and any content dependent on this data will be blocked from rendering until the request completes.

User interactivity (INP) is poor due to a long-running script task that blocks the main thread for 233ms. This task occurs around 3.2 seconds after page load and is initiated by a `setTimeout`. The resulting 255ms Long Animation Frame exceeds the 'good' threshold and will cause noticeable lag for any user trying to interact with the page at that moment.
suggestions.implementation:
- Profile the execution of `app.js` during the initial page load to identify the specific function causing the long task. Refactor this function by breaking its work into smaller, asynchronous chunks. Each chunk should run for less than 50ms before yielding to the main thread using techniques like `setTimeout(..., 0)`, `requestIdleCallback`, or by moving the computation to a Web Worker.
- Modify the JavaScript that initiates the request to `api.github.com`. If the data is not essential for the initial view, fetch it asynchronously after the main page content has loaded (e.g., after the `load` event). If the data is essential, render a placeholder or loading skeleton UI first, and then fetch the data on the client-side to populate the view. This will unblock the initial page paint.
- Locate the function being called by `setTimeout` that executes around the 3.2-second mark. Profile this function to identify the source of the heavy computation. Refactor the code to break the work into smaller chunks, each taking less than 50ms to execute. Use `async`/`await` with a helper function that yields to the main thread, or chain smaller tasks using `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
suggestions.title: Break up initial long-running script to improve interactivity

suggestions.description:
The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) is being delayed because images visible in the initial viewport are incorrectly marked with `loading="lazy"`. This attribute tells the browser to defer loading the image until it's needed, which is counter-productive for critical, above-the-fold content. The download of the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) image is not prioritized, causing it to compete for bandwidth with less critical resources. While several images might be in the viewport, only one will be the final LCP element. Giving this element a high priority ensures it's downloaded as early as possible.
suggestions.implementation: - Review the images in the initial mobile viewport. In your HTML, remove the `loading="lazy"` attribute from all `` tags that are visible without scrolling. This will allow the browser to discover and load these critical images earlier, significantly improving LCP. - Once you have identified the primary LCP image (e.g., the main hero image or banner, likely one of `img.h-80.w-80` or `img.h-full.w-full`), add the `fetchpriority="high"` attribute to its `` tag. This signals to the browser to download this image with high priority, ahead of other resources.

suggestions.description:
The Botpress chat widget is severely impacting both LCP and INP. Its scripts (`inject.js`, `index.17558395.js`) and stylesheet (`inject.css`) are render-blocking, and its execution causes a 441ms long task that freezes the main thread. The widget also contains 764KB of unused JavaScript code during initial load.

The page loads multiple, redundant analytics and tag manager scripts (`gtm.js`, `gtag/js` twice, `analytics.js`), contributing a combined 752KB of unused code and causing long tasks that harm INP. Long tasks of 388ms (from `G-M2XJX47YPY`) and 173ms (from `UA-119155027-6`) were directly attributed to these scripts, blocking the main thread.
suggestions.implementation:
- To fix this, defer the entire chat widget's loading until a user interacts with a chat-related element (e.g., a 'Chat with us' button). Remove the current script and stylesheet tags from the document `<head>`. Instead, use JavaScript to dynamically append the tags for `inject.js` and `inject.css` from `cdn.botpress.cloud` only after a user clicks the button. Applying `loading='lazy'` to the widget's iframe is another effective approach.
- Consolidate all tracking logic into a single Google Tag Manager container (e.g., `GTM-K8P5P8FQ`). Remove the direct script tags for Google Analytics (`analytics.js`) and the redundant `gtag/js` scripts. Then, audit the GTM container to remove any unused or redundant tags, triggers, and variables. Defer non-essential tracking tags to fire after the `load` event or on user interaction to reduce their impact on initial load.
suggestions.title: Lazy-load the third-party Botpress chat widget

suggestions.implementation: Configure your build process (e.g., Webpack, Rollup, Vite) to aggressively tree-shake and code-split `/dist/bundle.js`. The goal is to create smaller, route-specific chunks and completely eliminate the 1190KB of unused code identified by coverage reports. Only the JavaScript essential for the initial page view should be loaded synchronously.

suggestions.description: The page's Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) is severely delayed by over 1000ms because the server uses the outdated HTTP/1.1 protocol. This limits the browser to a few parallel connections, causing dozens of critical CSS and JavaScript files to be queued and wait for over 900ms before they even start downloading. This will allow the browser to download dozens of assets in parallel over a single connection, eliminating the extensive 'Blocked' time shown in network waterfalls and dramatically speeding up the initial load.

suggestions.description:
The page loads two versions of jQuery. The version from `lib.sinaapp.com` is render-blocking and takes over 2.3 seconds to load, severely delaying LCP by more than 2300ms. Removing this redundant script is the single largest and easiest LCP improvement available.

The page makes two render-blocking requests to the third-party domain `fonts.useso.com` to fetch CSS for the 'PT Serif' and 'PT Sans' fonts. This external dependency slows down the critical rendering path and introduces a potential point of failure.
suggestions.implementation:
- In the main HTML document, find and delete the `<script>` tag that loads `jquery-1.9.1.min.js` from `//lib.sinaapp.com/js/jquery/1.9.1/jquery-1.9.1.min.js`. The page already includes a local jQuery version at `/javascripts/libs/jquery.min.js`, making this external call unnecessary.
- Download the WOFF2 font files for 'PT Serif' and 'PT Sans'. Remove the two `<link>` tags that request CSS from `fonts.useso.com`. Host the font files on your own server and declare them directly in your main stylesheet (`screen.css`) using `@font-face` rules. Ensure each `@font-face` rule includes `font-display: swap` to prevent text rendering from being blocked.
suggestions.title: Remove redundant and slow third-party jQuery library

suggestions.description: The scripts `modernizr-2.0.js` and `octopress.js` are loaded synchronously in the document `<head>`, which blocks the browser from parsing the page and rendering content, delaying LCP. Additionally, `modernizr-2.0.js` causes a 299ms long task, which harms TBT and INP.
suggestions.implementation: In the main HTML document, add the `defer` attribute to the `<script>` tags for `/javascripts/modernizr-2.0.js` and `/javascripts/octopress.js`. This will cause them to load in parallel with HTML parsing and execute only after the document is fully parsed, unblocking the initial render.
suggestions.title: Defer non-critical JavaScript to unblock rendering

suggestions.description: The server is using a legacy HTTP/1.x protocol for first-party assets, which causes head-of-line blocking and slows down resource loading. This is a root cause that negatively impacts the download speed of numerous critical resources, delaying LCP.
suggestions.implementation: Configure the web server (e.g., Apache, Nginx) and/or CDN to serve all first-party traffic over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3. This will enable multiplexing and reduce connection overhead, speeding up resource delivery across the entire site.
suggestions.title: Enable HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 to accelerate resource delivery

suggestions.description:
Multiple above-the-fold images, including potential LCP elements, are missing `width` and `height` attributes. This prevents the browser from reserving space for them, leading to significant layout shifts (CLS) when the images load and push content down. Affected elements include `img.img-fluid` (src: `images/homepage/simpleitk-logo-final.svg`) and `img.example-images` (src: `images/homepage/imageAsSpatialObjectConcept.png`).

Several extremely large images are severely delaying LCP due to excessive file sizes and download times. The image `segmentation-1.png` is 861 KB and takes 12.9 seconds to download, and `spores.png` is 560 KB taking 11.8 seconds. Other images like `iowa.png` (171 KB) are also unnecessarily large.
suggestions.implementation: - For all `` elements identified in the findings, add explicit `width` and `height` attributes corresponding to the intrinsic size of the image file. To maintain responsiveness, ensure your CSS includes `height: auto;` and `max-width: 100%;` for these images. This will prevent CLS by allowing the browser to reserve the correct aspect ratio for the image space before it loads. - Optimize the following images by resizing them to their display dimensions, compressing them, and converting them to a modern format like WebP or AVIF: `segmentation-1.png`, `spores.png`, `iowa.png`, `nlm.jpg`, and `monash_university.png`. If any of these images are below the fold, also add the `loading="lazy"` attribute to defer their download.
suggestions.title: Add `width` and `height` attributes to images to prevent layout shifts (CLS)

suggestions.description: A very long animation frame is blocking the main thread for 1258ms at the very beginning of the page load. This severe blockage delays rendering (FCP, LCP) and makes the page completely unresponsive, leading to a poor INP score.
suggestions.implementation: Use the browser's performance profiler to identify the specific JavaScript function or script causing the 1258ms long task at page start. Once identified, refactor the code to break the work into smaller chunks using techniques like `requestIdleCallback` or `setTimeout(..., 0)` to yield to the main thread and prevent it from freezing.
suggestions.title: Break up 1258ms main-thread blocking task to improve interactivity and LCP

suggestions.description:
An extremely long-running JavaScript task executes for 7.5 seconds at the very beginning of the page load. This freezes the main thread, completely blocking rendering and preventing any user interaction, severely impacting LCP, FCP, and INP.

A long-running script, triggered by the `DOMContentLoaded` event, blocks the main thread for 867ms. This makes the page unresponsive to user input during a critical loading phase, resulting in a poor INP score. Analysis suggests a function like `deepCopyObject` within `prototypePost.js` may be a key contributor.
suggestions.implementation:
- Use the browser's performance profiler to identify the specific script and function(s) causing the 7.5-second task at page load. Once identified, this code must be refactored to either be broken into smaller asynchronous chunks using `setTimeout`, deferred until after the page is interactive, or moved off the main thread to a web worker.
- Identify the function bound to the 'DOMContentLoaded' event that is causing the 867ms task. Refactor this function by breaking its work into smaller, asynchronous chunks. Use `setTimeout(..., 0)` or `requestIdleCallback` to yield control back to the main thread between chunks, improving page responsiveness.
suggestions.title: Fix 7.5-second JavaScript task that freezes the page at load

suggestions.description:
The page's rendering is blocked by 6 synchronous scripts in the <head>, including large files like `prototypePost.js` and `data.js`. These scripts must be downloaded and executed before the browser can paint any content, significantly delaying LCP and FCP.

The initial render is blocked by 7 stylesheets in the <head>, including `styles.css` (133 KB), which takes over 3.5 seconds to download. This 'render-blocking' CSS prevents the browser from displaying any content until all files are downloaded and parsed, severely delaying FCP and LCP.
suggestions.implementation:
- Add the `defer` attribute to the <script> tags for all 6 non-essential JavaScript files loaded in the <head>. This includes `jquery-1.7.1.min.js`, `jquery-ui-1.8.10.custom.min.js`, `data/document.js`, `resources/scripts/prototypePre.js`, `data.js` and `resources/scripts/prototypePost.js`. This will allow the browser to parse the HTML and start rendering the page while the scripts download in the background.
- Identify the minimal CSS rules required to style the above-the-fold content. Inline these 'critical' styles directly into a `<style>` block in the `<head>` of the HTML. Then, load the full stylesheets (like `styles.css` and the font files) asynchronously by using `<link rel="preload" as="style" onload="this.onload=null;this.rel='stylesheet'">` pattern.
suggestions.title: Defer render-blocking JavaScript files to accelerate initial paint

suggestions.description: The page has a CLS score of 1.14, largely because 20 image elements, including potential LCP candidates like `img#u0_img`, are missing `width` and `height` attributes. This causes the page layout to shift and reflow as each image loads, creating a poor user experience.
suggestions.implementation: Add explicit `width` and `height` attributes to all 20 `` elements identified in the HTML analysis, such as `img#u0_img` (src: `images/index/u0.png`) and `img#u2_img` (src: `images/index/u2.png`). This allows the browser to reserve the correct amount of space for the images before they are downloaded, preventing layout shifts.
suggestions.title: Add width and height attributes to all images to prevent layout shifts

suggestions.description:
The main stylesheet, `nicepage.css`, is 1.45 MB and takes over 15 seconds to download, blocking the entire page from rendering. This is the primary cause of the extremely high LCP of 16.2 seconds, as identified in finding har-lcp-1.

An extremely long animation frame freezes the main thread for 16 seconds at the start of page load, making the page unresponsive and delaying LCP. This is caused by the synchronous parsing and execution of large JavaScript files, particularly `nicepage.js` (351 KB).
suggestions.implementation:
- Identify the CSS rules required for the initial, above-the-fold content. Inline these critical styles in a `<style>` block in the document `<head>`. Load the full `nicepage.css` stylesheet asynchronously by changing its `link` tag to `<link rel="stylesheet" href="nicepage.css" media="print" onload="this.media='all'">`. As a further optimization, use a tool to audit and remove unused CSS from `nicepage.css` to reduce its overall size.
- Add the `defer` attribute to the `<script>` tags for `nicepage.js` and `jquery.js`. This will ensure the scripts are downloaded in parallel but their execution is deferred until after the HTML has been parsed, unblocking the initial render and improving interactivity. Example: `<script src="nicepage.js" defer></script>`. This change directly addresses the root cause of the 16-second freeze.
suggestions.title: Extract Critical CSS from `nicepage.css` and Defer Non-Critical Styles

suggestions.description: All 8 LCP candidate images, including `images/16.jpg` and `images/counter-top.jpg`, are missing `width` and `height` attributes in the HTML. This forces the browser to reflow the page after images load, causing significant Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS).
suggestions.implementation: For each `` element on the page, add `width` and `height` attributes that match the intrinsic dimensions of the image file. This allows the browser to reserve the correct space for the image before it downloads, preventing the layout shift. For example: ``.
suggestions.title: Add Explicit Dimensions to Images to Prevent Layout Shifts

suggestions.description: The main JavaScript files, `nicepage.js` and `jquery.js`, contain a combined 339 KB of unused code that is downloaded, parsed, and compiled on page load. This contributes to long script execution times (e.g., a 329ms task), blocking the main thread and harming Interaction to Next Paint (INP).
suggestions.implementation: Use a bundler with tree-shaking capabilities (like Webpack or Rollup) to analyze `nicepage.js` and `jquery.js` and automatically remove the unused code identified in the coverage reports. For jQuery, if it cannot be removed entirely, consider creating a custom build that includes only the modules your site uses.
suggestions.title: Remove Unused JavaScript Code to Reduce Execution Time

suggestions.description:
The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) is being severely delayed by its image element, `fundo-oldschool.jpg`. This 925 KB image takes nearly 6 seconds to download, consuming excessive bandwidth and preventing the LCP from rendering promptly.

The current LCP element, `span.et_parallax_bg.et_pb_parallax_css`, is rendered using a CSS `background-image`. This prevents the browser's preload scanner from discovering the image early, delaying its download and the LCP time.
suggestions.implementation: - In your media library or codebase, find the image `fundo-oldschool.jpg`. Resize it to match its display dimensions on the page. Compress it using a tool like Squoosh or ImageOptim and convert it to a modern format like WebP or AVIF. Aim for a file size under 150 KB. - Modify the theme's template file to replace the `` that uses a CSS background with a standard `` tag. Set the `src` to the image URL (`fundo-oldschool.jpg`). Add `fetchpriority="high"` and `loading="eager"` to the `` tag to signal its importance to the browser. Ensure it has `width` and `height` attributes to prevent layout shift.
suggestions.title: Compress and resize the LCP image `fundo-oldschool.jpg`

suggestions.description: A massive 1.3MB JavaScript file from Font Awesome (`all.js`) is loaded synchronously in the document head. This blocks the browser from rendering the page for over 2 seconds, severely impacting First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Largest Contentful Paint (LCP).
suggestions.implementation: Locate the `<script>` tag for `https://use.fontawesome.com/releases/v5.0.8/js/all.js`. Add the `defer` attribute to it. This will allow the browser to download the script without blocking page rendering, and the script will execute after the HTML document has been parsed.
suggestions.title: Defer the render-blocking 1.3MB Font Awesome script

suggestions.description: The page has a very high Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) score of 0.46. This is caused by text and other elements shifting when web fonts (like 'Open Sans') replace the initial system fonts. The largest shift displaces content by nearly 300px.
suggestions.implementation: To stabilize the layout during font loading, use the CSS Font Metrics Override descriptors. For each `@font-face` rule, generate and add `ascent-override`, `descent-override`, and `size-adjust` values that match the fallback font's metrics to the web font's metrics. Tools like the 'Font Style Matcher' can help calculate these values.
suggestions.title: Prevent layout shift from web font loading

suggestions.description: The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) is severely delayed by an unoptimized 8.6 MB image, `Pope-peter_pprubens.jpg`, hosted on `upload.wikimedia.org`. Its download time of over 44 seconds, as reported in network logs, completely stalls page rendering and is the most significant performance bottleneck.
suggestions.implementation: Resize the image `Pope-peter_pprubens.jpg` to match its display dimensions on the page. Compress it using a modern format like WebP or AVIF, aiming for a file size under 300KB. Replace the current image source in the HTML with this new, optimized version.
suggestions.title: Optimize Extremely Large 8.6 MB Image Blocking LCP

suggestions.description: A long animation frame blocks the main thread for 899ms at the start of page load. This is caused by a large 65KB inline script executing synchronously, which contains 23KB of code that only runs after the page has loaded. This severely delays rendering (FCP, LCP) and makes the page unresponsive, leading to poor Interaction to Next Paint (INP).
suggestions.implementation: Identify the JavaScript functions within the large inline script that can be executed after the initial page render. Move the 23KB of code identified as 'post-LCP' functionality into a separate file. Load this new file asynchronously using a `<script defer>` tag or by dynamically inserting the script after the `load` event to unblock the main thread.
suggestions.title: Break Up Initial Long Task to Improve Interactivity and LCP
